Every semester I invite four or five guest speakers to my marketing course. People often ask me: how do you choose them? It's simple. First, I ask: what have you done? I want people who have worked on real projects, who have launched campaigns and made mistakes. Second, I ask: have you ever taught before? Many of my best guests have never taught. That's fine. I just ask them to prepare a short slide deck, bring one good case study, and leave twenty minutes to take questions. Last year a guest from a startup gave the best class of the semester. She had no teaching experience, but the students loved her stories.

Hi, it's Priya again. Have you ever taught a class? I have, but only three times. The first time was last March, at a university in Pune. It was a workshop about marketing data for thirty students. I was very nervous. I've given many presentations at work, but students are a different audience. They ask a lot of questions! I prepared too many slides, and I didn't finish. But the case study worked very well. The students analyzed the data of a real online store, and they loved it. Since then, I've taught two more workshops. I've never given a full course, but maybe next year.
